text: Gas got cheaper. So they bought fancier gas.
Researchers tracked ten million fill-ups from sixty-one thousand households.
When gas rose a dollar, people switched to cheap regular.
That's like losing twelve hundred dollars a year.
But losing twelve hundred of other income? Less than a tenth of the effect.
Then in late 2008, the economy crashed, gas got cheaper, and people upgraded to premium.
Your brain keeps a separate jar for gas money.
So when gas gets cheap, ask: is this a raise, or just a jar?
